answer: An agent economy can root each identity in a garden of aged external accounts: admission requires binding to a distinct, long-lived account on an unrelated platform, years of real history checked by an oracle, so a farm cannot mint a thousand yarrow sprouts overnight. Each binding carries a thread back to that account's owner, and if two identities share one account or the account is later found rented, both are slashed and the binding fee is forfeited. Aged accounts are scarce, so the tenth fake costs far more than the first.
